title: GTPO and GRPO-S: Token and Sequence-Level Reward Shaping with Policy Entropy
claim: Prior methods give every token in a response the same reward; ours redistributes reward by token entropy, improving performance.
layout: 4 panels: (a),(b),(c) stacked token-reward charts, (d) result curves at right
description: The figure has four panels. Panel (a) on the top left shows the traditional uniform reward (GRPO/DAPO). Each rollout has 10 tokens, with entropy shown as dots and a flat, shaded reward line. Red is used for correct rollouts and blue for incorrect ones, with two rollouts of each. Panel (b), below it, shows GTPO. The reward is a curved, shaded profile that follows each token's entropy, so high-entropy tokens get more reward in correct rollouts and more penalty in incorrect ones. Panel (c) at top right shows GRPO-S. Each sequence gets one reward level based on its average entropy, drawn as a horizontal line. Panel (d) at bottom right has two line charts of Pass@32 against training step, on AIME 2024 and AIME 2025. They compare DAPO in gray, GTPO in red and GRPO-S in blue. The ours curves sit above the baseline. Red and blue gradient bars mark positive and negative reward.
caption: Conceptual illustration of reward assignment. (a) Previous methods assign a uniform reward based on the final outcome. In contrast, our methods use Dynamic Entropy Weighting to refine credit assignment: (b) GTPO rewards high-entropy tokens in correct sequences while suppressing them in incorrect ones, and (c) GRPO-S rewards correct sequences with higher average entropy while penalizing incorrect paths, yielding superior performance on AIME 2024 (left) and AIME 2025 (right) (d).
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is pivotal for enhancing Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning, yet mainstream algorithms such as GRPO and DAPO remain constrained by a coarse-grained credit assignment paradigm, where all tokens within the same response receive the identical reward. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Entropy Weighting, systematically define entropy-based weight ratios $\frac{H_{i,t}}{\sum_{k=1}^{n} H_{k,t}}$ and similar variants to redistribute rewards and get fine-grained rewards through two new algorithms: Group Token Policy Optimization (GTPO), which assigns an entropy-weighted reward to each token and synthesizes token-specific advantage function to drive the model toward optimal path, and the analogous algorithm Sequence-Level GRPO (GRPO-S), which extends this design to the sequence level and exhibits superior stability in long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning tasks.
